claim: Can a translation shim re-emit run_adapter_dispatch's event stream as the §12.3 typed SSE protocol with ZERO engine/route changes (D-17's 'no engine work, old route untouched' premise)?
reality: NO. A pure wire-level translation shim can re-LABEL the events that already exist (start→turn.open, data-stage→phase, data-tool→activity, text-delta→block.delta, finish→turn.commit/close), but it CANNOT satisfy §12.3's load-bearing ordering requirement: 'The stream opens immediately on POST. turn.open and phase{plan,start} go out before the planner runs' (arch doc:1545-1547), which §19.7 makes a GATE PASS CONDITION ('Work is visible immediately | POST → turn.open < 300 ms; first activity < 1 s', arch doc:3173). Today NO SSE stream exists until runAdapterDispatch is invoked at route.ts:988 — AFTER the planner (route.ts:436-454) and AFTER tool fetch (route.ts:752-798). The first wire byte is written at run_adapter_dispatch.ts:294. Worse, the planner-fault path returns a NON-STREAMING NextResponse.json(...,{status:422}) at route.ts:447-450, and bundle validation returns another 422 at route.ts:803-806 — both structurally mutually exclusive with an already-open stream (you cannot set a 422 status after streaming headers are flushed). To emit turn.open before planning you MUST (a) hoist createUIMessageStream to the top of the route, (b) move planner+tool-fetch INSIDE the stream execute body, and (c) convert BOTH 422 bail-outs into in-stream error events. That is a restructuring of the OLD ROUTE — the exact thing D-17 says stays 'untouched'. Therefore D-17's core premise is FALSE for the single event the whole 'kill the dead air / feel like Claude Code' bet depends on. The render/client half of the bet IS cheap (see PG1-C2-0006); the SSE-protocol half is not shimmable.

claim: Can activity.upsert be synthesized from the existing toolEventLog + stage parts, or does it need new engine instrumentation (sub-question 4)?
reality: PARTIAL — shape yes, semantics+timing no. The raw fields exist: toolEventLog carries {name,status,ms,ok_count,err_count} (run_adapter_dispatch.ts:109) and data-stage carries stage/status/ms. A shim CAN emit activity-shaped rows from them. But §12.3's activity.upsert is defined as {activity_id, kind, label_key, status, ms?, counts?, detail_ref?} with an explicit 'keyed upsert — NEVER a new row per update' contract (arch doc:1508-1510). Two hard gaps: (1) TIMING — the ENTIRE toolEventLog is dumped in one synchronous loop at synthesis-start (run_adapter_dispatch.ts:297-303), AFTER planner and tool fetch have already completed; nothing is emitted WHILE a tool runs. §19.7 requires 'first activity < 1 s' (arch doc:3173); today the first activity cannot appear until planning+retrieval finish (multi-second). Delivering live activities requires moving emission into the tool-fetch loop, which lives in route.ts:752 — the untouched route. (2) LABEL — data-tool carries the raw tool `name` only (run_adapter_dispatch.ts:300); there is no label_key or reader_label. §12.8 requires label_key→reader_label from the registry (§8.7). Lane R-1's audit found that reader-label projection is a category gap. So activity.upsert is synthesizable in SHAPE but not in the two properties (live timing, reader label) that the gate and D-15 actually require — both need new instrumentation outside the dispatch module.

claim: Can citation sentinels / citation.define be introduced by a prompt change alone, or does the gate code itself need modification (sub-question 5)?
reality: NO — prompt-alone is necessary but not sufficient. Today citation_check.ts operates ENTIRELY post-stream: it regex-counts SIG.MSR.NNN ids already present in the finished text (Layer 1, citation_check.ts:14,37-41) and cross-references them against the context JSON (Layer 2, validateCitations @93-146). It NEVER rewrites a sentinel or emits a mid-stream anchor. The §12.9/§12.9.1 design requires the model to emit ⟦cite: SIG.MSR.413⟧ sentinels AND the SERVER to rewrite them to ⟦n⟧ + emit a citation.define event BEFORE any byte reaches the client (arch doc:1715-1716), with a 64-byte/400ms hold-back buffer for sentinels split across delta boundaries (arch doc:1730-1745, A-23). The prompt change produces the sentinels; but the rewriter+hold-back buffer must be injected INTO the delta loop at run_adapter_dispatch.ts:321-331, where text_delta is currently written raw and immediately to the wire (line 329) with no interception. That is new streaming-path code inside the dispatch module. §12.9.1 itself confirms the existing gate is RETAINED and merely re-pointed ('Existing prescriptive-class ERROR citation_check.ts:91,129-135 — retained, re-pointed at citation parts', arch doc:1770), i.e. the gate stays AND a new rewriter is added alongside. Confirmed: not a prompt-only change; requires a server-side streaming sentinel rewriter with buffering, plus tolerant grammar and per-model hallucination counters (§12.9.1).

claim: Can client-side stable-prefix segmentation (A-21/§12.4) work with the CURRENT markdown stack, or does it need a new parser (sub-question 6)?
reality: YES — this is the ONE cleanly-green sub-answer. The client already renders assistant text through Streamdown v2.5.0 (MarkdownContent.tsx:4 `import { Streamdown } from 'streamdown'`, remark-gfm+remark-math plugins @186), a streaming-markdown renderer purpose-built for progressive block rendering with incomplete-construct tolerance and block memoization — exactly the A-21/§12.4 'one markdown engine, freeze every block except the last, memoize frozen subtrees' design. MarkdownContent is already memoized (memo @202). So the render/client HALF of the D-17 bet (settled content never moves, caret discipline, block-level freeze) is largely ALREADY IMPLEMENTED and needs no new parser. CAVEAT: A-21 mandates 'one markdown engine in the system' but package.json ships BOTH streamdown ^2.5.0 AND react-markdown ^10.1.0 — a consolidation task, not a build-from-scratch. This confirms D-17's INSTINCT that the render bet is the cheap part to prove; the problem is that the render bet is NOT where the risk lives — the SSE-protocol/route-reorder half is (PG1-C2-0001).

claim: Honest time estimate for the P0' shim (sub-question 7). Is it D-17's claimed 3-4 weeks?
reality: NO — not as scoped ('disposable shim, no planner work, old route untouched, 3-4 weeks'). Breakdown against §19.7's actual gate rows: (A) Event re-labeling shim (start→turn.open, data-stage→phase, data-tool→activity shape, text→block, finish→turn.commit/close): ~3-5 days, genuinely cheap. (B) Client render bet (freeze/caret/memoize): mostly DONE via Streamdown — ~3-5 days to wire + consolidate react-markdown (PG1-C2-0006). (C) Early turn.open <300ms + first activity <1s: REQUIRES route reorder (hoist stream creation, move planner+tool-fetch into execute body, convert two 422 bail-outs to in-stream errors) — ~1 week AND violates 'old route untouched' (PG1-C2-0001, -0004). (D) citation.define sentinel pipeline (server hold-back rewriter + tolerant grammar + hallucination counters, §12.9.1): ~1-1.5 weeks new streaming-path code (PG1-C2-0005). (E) activity.upsert live-emission + reader-label registry projection: ~1 week, R-1 category gap (PG1-C2-0004). (F) Typed writer protocol removing six `as any` + reasoning open/close lifecycle: ~3-5 days (PG1-C2-0007). (G) Gate's lower rows — 'survives bad networks: 1-byte trickle, 50KB slabs, 3s stalls, mid-block disconnect, reconnect-and-replay' + mobile fixture suite + screen-reader axe-core: §16.6 verifies reconnection/replay substrate is ABSENT (last_event_seq stored but never consumed) and mobile is PARTIAL — this is multi-week net-new test+resilience infrastructure, ~2-3 weeks. HONEST TOTAL for the gate AS WRITTEN: ~6-9 weeks, and it necessarily touches consult/route.ts and the dispatch delta loop. The 3-4 week figure is achievable ONLY if the gate is descoped to 'client renders the existing post-planning stream nicely' — which fails §19.7's first row (work visible immediately / turn.open<300ms) because the stream still opens after planning. The core render bet CAN be cheaply proven; the 'feels like Claude Code / no dead air' bet cannot, and that is the bet D-17 says P0' exists to prove.
